# Unix listener parameters

This reference lists all parameters of the `unix` listener stanza. For a conceptual overview, refer to [Unix listener](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners/unix).

```hcl
listener "unix" {
  purpose = "api"
  address = "/var/run/boundary-api.sock"
}
```

## General parameters

- `purpose` `(string: <required>)` - Specifies the purpose of the listener. Can be `api`, `cluster`, or `ops`.

- `address` `(string: "")` - Specifies the address as a filesystem path to bind the socket to for listening.

- `http_idle_timeout` `(string: "5m")` - Specifies the maximum amount of time to wait for the next request when keep-alives are enabled. If `http_idle_timeout` is zero, the value of `http_read_timeout` is used. If both are zero, the value of `http_read_header_timeout` is used. Specify using a duration suffix such as `"30s"` or `"1h"`.

- `http_read_header_timeout` `(string: "10s")` - Specifies the amount of time allowed to read request headers. Specify using a duration suffix such as `"30s"` or `"1h"`.

- `http_read_timeout` `(string: "30s")` - Specifies the maximum duration for reading the entire request, including the body. Specify using a duration suffix such as `"30s"` or `"1h"`.

- `http_write_timeout` `(string: "0")` - Specifies the maximum duration before timing out a response write. Boundary resets the timeout whenever it reads the header of a new request. The default value of `"0"` means no timeout. Specify using a duration suffix such as `"30s"` or `"1h"`.

- `max_request_duration` `(string: "90s")` - Specifies the maximum duration allowed for a request before Boundary cancels it. This overrides `default_max_request_duration` for this listener.

- `cors_enabled` `(boolean: true)` - Specifies whether CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) is enabled. CORS lets Boundary support external browser-based clients such as Boundary Desktop Client. If not specified, CORS is enabled with an allowed origin that grants access to Boundary Desktop Client, unless overridden with `cors_disable_default_allowed_origin_values`.

- `cors_disable_default_allowed_origin_values` `(boolean: false)` - Specifies that Boundary should not append default allowed origin values, such as the origin of Boundary Desktop Client, to any values specified in `cors_allowed_origins`. This also disables the behavior of enabling CORS when `cors_enabled` is not specified.

- `cors_allowed_origins` `(array(string): ["serve://boundary"])` - Specifies an array of allowed CORS origins. Origins must include protocol, host, and port when the port differs from the default for the specified protocol. To allow all origins, set to `['*']`. By default, Boundary appends the origin of Boundary Desktop Client, `serve://boundary`, to any values included here, unless `cors_disable_default_allowed_origin_values` is specified.

- `cors_allowed_headers` `(array(string): [])` - Specifies an array of headers that are permitted on cross-origin requests. These headers are appended to the list that Boundary allows by default, such as `"Content-Type"`, `"X-Requested-With"`, and `"Authorization"`.

## TLS parameters

The TLS parameters are valid for `api` and `ops` listeners. The `cluster` connection uses its own ephemeral TLS stack. Refer to [TLS in Boundary](/boundary/docs/secure/encryption/connections-tls) for more information. For an example, refer to [Configure TLS for listeners](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners/configure-tls).

- `tls_disable` `(string: "false")` - Specifies whether TLS is disabled. Boundary assumes TLS by default; set to `"true"` to opt in to insecure communication.

- `tls_cert_file` `(string: <required-if-enabled, reloads-on-SIGHUP>)` - Specifies the path to the certificate for TLS. To use a CA certificate, concatenate the primary certificate and the CA certificate into one file. The primary certificate must appear first. On `SIGHUP`, Boundary reloads the certificate from the path set at startup. Changing this value while Boundary is running has no effect on a reload.

- `tls_key_file` `(string: <required-if-enabled, reloads-on-SIGHUP>)` - Specifies the path to the private key for the certificate. If the key file is encrypted, Boundary prompts for the passphrase at startup. The passphrase must remain the same between key files when reloading. On `SIGHUP`, Boundary reloads the key from the path set at startup. Changing this value while Boundary is running has no effect on a reload.

- `tls_min_version` `(string: "tls12")` - Specifies the minimum supported version of TLS. Accepted values are `"tls12"` and `"tls13"`.

- `tls_max_version` `(string: "tls13")` - Specifies the maximum supported version of TLS. Useful when upstream appliances such as load balancers do not yet support newer versions. Accepted values are `"tls12"` and `"tls13"`.

- `tls_cipher_suites` `(string: "")` - Overrides the default list of supported cipher suites with a comma-delimited list. The list of available cipher suites is in the [Go TLS documentation](https://golang.org/src/crypto/tls/cipher_suites.go).

- `tls_prefer_server_cipher_suites` `(string: "false")` - Specifies that the server's cipher suite preferences take precedence over the client's.

- `tls_require_and_verify_client_cert` `(string: "false")` - Enables client certificate authentication. The listener requires a client certificate that validates against the CA specified in `tls_client_ca_file`, or against the system CAs if `tls_client_ca_file` is not set.

- `tls_client_ca_file` `(string: "")` - Specifies the path to a PEM-encoded CA file that Boundary uses to verify client certificates.
